SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SPELLING INSTRUCTION BE ABLE TO:
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Spelling instruction be able to: helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: SPELLING INSTRUCTION BE ABLE TO:
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

What this means

How to learn it

In this part you learn to apply rules of spelling patterns to themes i.e.(sing the song avocado, in writing papaya, banana x2 fruits are lif. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply rules of spelling patterns to themes i.e.(sing the song avocado, in writing papaya, banana x2 fruits are lif.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply rules of spelling patterns to themes i.e.(sing the song avocado, in writing papaya, banana x2 fruits are lif. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Spelling instruction be able to: is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Spelling instruction be able to: to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use a range of spelling  Learners practice sorting words according to strategies to correct given patterns. misspelled words  Learners use reinforcement activities to relate.
3. Practise this skill: apply rules of spelling patterns to themes i.e.(sing the song avocado, in writing papaya, banana x2 fruits are lif.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Spelling instruction be able to: from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Spelling instruction be able to:: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Spelling instruction be able to:?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Spelling instruction be able to: means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use a range of spelling  Learners practice sorting words according to strategies to correct given patterns. misspelled words  Learners use reinforcement activities to relate.
